_README.what: The thirty-five quests of Whispering Lake: a kid, five dollars, Walt, and the truth about Old Whisper.
_README.voices: Walt's lines are in `lines`, keyed by cue id, and recorded to audio/ by tools/record.js. The player's line in `player` is spoken by the system voice for accessibility. `nudge` is what Walt says when you come back without the job done.
_README.mechanics: Fish are tagged and released - a fish quest counts tags, never keeps. `stage` is the vessel whose water the quest is in, and the water gates the quest. `needs` are the quests that must be finished first.
_README.workflow: Edit in editor.html, then run tools/build_content.py.

quests.title: The First Dollar
quests.card: Scoop 30 minnows and shiners for Walt's survey tank
quests.player: I want to become a real fisherman!

say.brief: Well, hey there, kid! Welcome to Whispering Lake Research and Tackle. Don't see many new faces down at the dock this early in the morning. Truth be told, I don't see many faces at all any more. Folks still buy their line and their hooks off me - I'm cheaper than town - but they don't fish here. Look out there. Not one boat on the water. Not any more. They'll tell you the lake's cursed. Something big out in the middle that takes the propeller clean off a boat. I stopped arguing about it years ago. So this is a research station now: I study what's in the water, and I write up what I find. And what I'd give to know what's down in the middle, where it drops past a hundred feet. Nobody's been out there and come back with anything but a story. Five bucks, huh? Everybody starts somewhere. What I need is a pair of young hands - we catch them, tag them, log them and put every one straight back. Nothing gets kept on my dock. Start me here: my survey tank's empty and I need to know what's growing along the shore this year. Take this hand net, scoop me up thirty minnows and shiners - a netful at a time - and I'll pay you twenty-five dollars cash. Deal? Hold on, one more thing before you go. Here's a map of the lake - take it, you're gonna need it. Whole thing's on there: the shoreline, the bay, the drop-off, and the deep water out in the middle. It won't tell you where the fish are. Nothing will. But it'll stop you getting turned around out there, and on this lake that matters.
say.nudge: No rush, kid. Thirty little fish - the shoreline's full of 'em. Dip the net where the water's knee-deep.
say.done: Look at all those minnows! Fantastic work, kid - that's my survey tank stocked for the season. Here's your twenty-five dollars cash, fair and square.

replies: I want to become a real fisherman!
What's out there?
Have you ever studied what's out in the middle?
I'd go out there and look for you... but all I've got is five dollars and no boat.
Deal.
Thanks, Walt.

quests.title: Panfish Tagging
quests.card: Catch, tag and release 3 Sunfish off the dock edge
quests.player: What should I buy first?

say.brief: You can use that money right now to buy this bamboo rod and a container of earthworms. Now, see these sunfish hanging around the dock? We don't keep 'em to eat - we tag 'em! Catch three sunfish, clip a field tag on their fin, and let 'em go. Bring me the tag data when you're done.
say.nudge: Three sunfish, tagged and let go. They're right under the boards.
say.done: Logbook updated! Excellent work. You've got a real gentle touch with those fish, kid.

quests.title: Perch Patrol
quests.card: Catch, tag and release 3 Yellow Perch from the dock pilings
quests.player: What fish are we logging next?

say.brief: Next up: yellow perch! They love hiding right next to the wooden dock pilings. Catch and tag three of 'em so we can track how fast they're growing this summer.
say.nudge: Perch hug those pilings. Three tags, and bring me the data.
say.done: Logbook updated! Perfect. Hey, while you're standing out on the dock, look down near the reed beds. Someone left a bunch of floating trash!

quests.title: Shoreline Clean-up
quests.card: Net 5 pieces of floating litter near the reeds
quests.player: I can clean that up right now.

say.brief: Grab your hand net and scoop out five pieces of litter. We keep this water clean so the baby fish have a safe place to grow.
say.nudge: That litter's still floating by the reeds. Five pieces, kid.
say.done: Thanks for clearing out that trash. The lake looks better already, and I put twelve bucks in your hand for the trouble.

quests.title: The Canoe Fund
quests.card: Tag and release 5 mixed panfish off the dock edge
quests.player: How do I get out onto the lake?

say.brief: You're moving fast, Junior Warden! Tag five more mixed panfish off the dock edge. Once that data's logged, you'll have enough cash to put a deposit down on my rental canoe and get off this dock!
say.nudge: Five more panfish and that canoe deposit is yours.
say.done: Five panfish tagged and logged - and that's your deposit money, kid. Twenty dollars puts the oars in your hands and that red canoe at the end of the slip is yours for the day. Say the word and she's yours.

quests.title: Weed Bed Bass
quests.card: Tag and release 2 Largemouth Bass under the lily pads
quests.player: Where is the best fishing spot in the bay?

say.brief: Head out into Shallow Bay, near the lily pads in fifteen feet of water. Largemouth bass love ambush hunting under those big green leaves. Tag two of 'em and bring back the log!
say.nudge: The bass are under the lily pads in fifteen feet. Two tags.
say.done: Two largemouth bass, healthy and tagged! Outstanding.

quests.title: Crappie Craze
quests.card: Tag and release 4 Black Crappies along the outer weed edge
quests.player: Where are the crappies hiding?

say.brief: Black crappies travel in schools near the outer weed edges in twenty feet of water. Paddle out steady, drop your line right along the weedline, and tag four of 'em for the sanctuary database.
say.nudge: Crappies run the outer weedline in twenty feet. Four of 'em.
say.done: Before you paddle back out, take this - Magnet Lure Number One! It attaches right to your line.

quests.title: The First Magnet Drop
quests.card: Haul up 3 pieces of scrap metal with Magnet Lure #1
quests.player: How does magnet fishing work?

say.brief: Drop it over the shallow scrap markers out in the bay. People have been dropping iron and lost gear in this lake for fifty years. Pull me up three pieces of scrap metal, and I'll clean those scuffs off your canoe for free!
say.nudge: Drop that magnet over the scrap markers. Three pieces gets your canoe cleaned.
say.done: Three good pieces of iron. Nice work with that magnet, kid.

quests.title: Mystery Clue #1: Something in the Weeds
quests.card: Magnet-fish near the west weeds and see what comes up
quests.player: I found it near the west weed beds!

say.brief: Big Mac lost something out by the west weed beds back in 2008 - swore blind a lake monster bit his boat, and he has never shut up about it since. Take the magnet out there and drag the bottom. I would dearly love to know what actually happened to that motor.
say.nudge: Whatever's out by the west weeds, the magnet'll find it.
say.done: Whoa! Hold on a second... where did you pull this up?! Look at those blade marks! This bronze propeller belonged to Big Mac's speedboat back in 2008. He used to tear through those shallow weeds like he owned the place, scaring off all the spawning bass. Big Mac swore a lake monster bit his boat! But look closely - Old Whisper didn't bite it. He jammed a thick, hardened tree root straight into the drive pin! Stopped his motor dead and taught Mac a lesson. Keep your eyes open out there, kid... I put that prop in the scrap bin - we can reuse that brass! Now, back to business.

quests.title: Big Bass Challenge
quests.card: Tag and release a Largemouth Bass over 5 lbs from the deep pads
quests.player: Are the big ones down in the deeper pads?

say.brief: There's a giant five-pound largemouth bass lurking in the deepest lily pads on the west side. Set your hook clean, tag her up, and let her go!
say.nudge: She's a five-pounder, in the deep pads - fourteen feet and down. Take your time.
say.done: Five pounds if she's an ounce, tagged and swimming. That's a proper bass, kid.

quests.title: Mystery Clue #2: Something in the Mud
quests.card: Magnet-fish the shallow drop-off — something's caught in the mud
quests.player: It was buried under thirty feet of mud.

say.brief: There's a shallow drop-off where the mud goes soft, and every so often somebody's magnet comes back heavier than it went down. Work that edge for me. Something metal is sitting in that mud, and I don't think it fell there on its own.
say.nudge: Something's in the mud at the shallow drop-off. Keep dragging that magnet.
say.done: What in the world... let me see that! It's caked in lake mud, but under the grime... that's solid brass. It looks like a frame for some old mechanical device. See these mounting brackets? I'm setting this right here on the corner of my workbench in a tray of oil to soak off the rust. Whatever this was... it didn't sink by accident. The sun's getting low over the trees, kid. Perfect timing for catfish!

quests.title: Night Night Catfish
quests.card: Tag and release 2 Channel Catfish along the muddy banks
quests.player: Where do catfish go when it gets dark?

say.brief: Channel catfish feed along the muddy shallow banks right around dusk. Get two of 'em tagged and logged before you head into the dock for the night.
say.nudge: Catfish come up the muddy banks at dusk. Two tags before dark.
say.done: Logbook updated! Nice catfish.

quests.title: Shallow Scrap Drive
quests.card: Trade 5 pieces of scrap metal to Walt at the counter
quests.player: What can I do with all this scrap metal?

say.brief: Hey, if you've got five pieces of scrap metal in your inventory from magnet-fishing, trade 'em to me at the counter. I'll give you fifty dollars of shop credit toward your gear!
say.nudge: Five pieces of scrap at the counter, and it's fifty dollars of credit.
say.done: You're doing great, kid. You're almost there!

quests.title: The Kayak Goal
quests.card: Tag and release 6 shallow bay fish
quests.player: How close am I to buying the Kayak?

say.brief: Tag and release six more shallow bay fish. Once that's logged, you'll have enough cash to buy your very own yellow Kayak! No more paying daily canoe rentals.
say.nudge: Six more bay fish and that kayak's yours.
say.done: That is the money, kid - enough for the kayak. She is tied up at the end of the boards whenever you are ready for her.

quests.title: Buying the Kayak
quests.card: Buy the yellow Kayak ($250)
quests.player: How deep can I go in this Kayak?

say.brief: She's all yours! That yellow Kayak is sleek, fast, and can handle deeper water. She'll easily take you past the thirty-five-foot drop-off. Just keep an eye on her hull durability bar down at the bottom of your screen. Hitting submerged logs out there will scuff her up, but you can always bring her back to me for repairs!
say.nudge: The yellow kayak's two hundred and fifty. Come see me at the counter.
say.done: Welcome to the Deep Hole, kid! The bottom drops like a cliff right past those buoys, all the way down to seventy-five feet.

replies: How deep can I go in this Kayak?
Thanks, Walt.

quests.title: Deep Waters
quests.card: Tag and release 2 Northern Pike off the drop-off
quests.player: What fish patrol the deep cliff ledges?

say.brief: Northern pike hang on the weed edge and follow the break down - thirty-five to forty-five feet is as deep as they go. Paddle out, work the edge, and tag two of them for me.
say.nudge: Pike patrol the rock ledges past the buoys. Two tags, kid.
say.done: Those northern pike put up a real fight, didn't they? Great tags.

quests.title: Catfish Depth
quests.card: Tag and release 3 Channel Catfish off the bottom at 40 ft
quests.player: Are there catfish down at fifty feet?

say.brief: Drop your line to the bottom in forty feet. Catfish are a warmwater fish - they hold on the mud above the cold layer and will not go down into it, whatever anybody tells you. Tag three of the big ones for me.
say.nudge: Straight down to the mud at forty feet. Three big catfish.
say.done: Three catfish off the mud and all three logged. You're getting the hang of the deep water.

quests.title: Breakline Walleye
quests.card: Tag two Walleye out on the breakline, 20 ft or deeper
quests.player: Where do walleye sit?

say.brief: Now then. There is a fish out on that breakline I have got no numbers on at all - walleye. Eyes like a cat's, feeds when the light goes flat, and gone the second the sun comes out. Twenty feet down off the drop, kid. Two of them tagged and I will have something to write in the column that has been empty since ninety-four.
say.nudge: Two walleye, out on the breakline, twenty feet down.
say.done: Walleye. Both tagged, both back in. That column is not empty any more, and it is your handwriting in it.

quests.title: Mystery Clue #3: More of the Same
quests.card: Magnet-fish the drop-off — there's more where that came from
quests.player: Do these gears belong to the brass frame?

say.brief: That brass frame has empty mountings in it, kid - whatever bolted into them is still down there. The drop-off is where the frame came from, so that's where the rest of it will be. Get the magnet down deep and drag it.
say.nudge: There's more of that brass down the drop-off. Keep the magnet down.
say.done: Aha! Look at this! These gear teeth match the brass frame you found earlier! Look - they interlock perfectly! Whoever built this knew exactly what they were doing. Let me mount these cogs right inside the frame...

quests.title: Kayak Care
quests.card: Repair the Kayak at the dock workshop
quests.player: How do I patch up the hull?

say.brief: You've been putting some miles on that kayak, kid! See those scuffs on the bottom? Bring her up to the dock workshop. A little resin patch and some scrap metal will have her running smooth again. Give it a shot!
say.nudge: Bring the kayak up to the workshop and we'll patch her.
say.done: Looks good as new!

quests.title: Pike Hunter
quests.card: Tag and release a Northern Pike over 10 lbs on the deep weed line
quests.player: Is there a trophy fish near the deep log jam?

say.brief: There is a ten-pounder working the outside weed line in forty feet of water - the old ones drop down the break as the day warms. Tag her and let her go, and mind your line.
say.nudge: Ten-pounder, on the outside weed line in forty feet. Keep him out of the pads.
say.done: A ten-pound pike off the deep weed edge! Tagged, logged and back in. That's the biggest thing in this lake with teeth - well, the biggest one anybody's ever landed.

quests.title: Mystery Clue #4: Something in the Log Jam
quests.card: Magnet-fish the deep log jam and see what comes up
quests.player: Why are the tines so thick and heavy?

say.brief: There's a log jam out in the deep water, and things collect in a log jam. If the rest of this machine went in where the frame did, the current will have walked it out that way. Take the magnet to the deep jam and see what comes up.
say.nudge: Try the magnet at the deep log jam. Something's still down there.
say.done: Kid... would you look at these. Fine little metal tines, packed in tight — that's not scrap, that's a comb out of a music box. Pluck one and it hums way down low, lower than anything I'd tune for a tune. This wasn't built to play for people. Somebody built this to talk to something underwater.

quests.title: Mystery Clue #5: The Deep Edge
quests.card: Haul something heavy up from the 75 ft edge
quests.player: What's down at seventy-five feet?

say.brief: Seventy-five feet, kid - the deep edge. The old Warden's station went down somewhere along there in the flood, and a station means records. That's heavy magnet work and a long haul up, but if there's anything left of ninety-four, that's where it is.
say.nudge: The seventy-five-foot edge, kid. Heavy magnet work.
say.done: Whoa — hold on, let me get a grip on that. That is heavy for a box that size. Would you look at that seal, stamped right into the lid. Lake Warden, nineteen ninety-four. This has been sitting down there since the flood took the station. There's a journal in here, kid. Water's got into it, but I can just make out the last page... 'The flood of ninety-four sank our underwater sanctuary station. My loyal sturgeon stayed behind to guard the baby fish. I call him...' ...and that's as far as I can get. Rest of the page is stuck together. Give me tonight to dry it out proper before it falls apart in my hands.

quests.title: Deep Trout Survey
quests.card: Tag and release 2 Lake Trout in 70 ft of cold water while Walt works on the journal
quests.player: Anything I can do while you work on that?

say.brief: While I work on that page, there's a survey I keep putting off. Lake trout - cold-water fish, down below the thermocline where it stays cold all summer, and they will not come up for anybody. Seventy feet, kid. Tag two of them for me and put them back, and I should have something to tell you in the morning.
say.nudge: Seventy feet, kid, down where it stays cold. Two lake trout - I'll be here with the journal.
say.done: Logbook updated! You're doing incredible work out there.

quests.title: The Dried Page
quests.card: Hear what Walt got off the Warden's last page
quests.player: Barnaby? So he's got a name.

say.brief: Kid! Dried that page out overnight, careful as I could. Warden's own hand, plain as day: 'I call him Barnaby.' Barnaby. That's not what you name a monster. Thirty years we've all been calling him Old Whisper, blaming him for every snapped line and every bad night out there — and near as I can tell, he's just an old sturgeon doing exactly what he was told to do back in ninety-four. Guarding this place. Which means whatever is left of that station is still out in the middle of this lake, and the middle is the one part of it neither of us can reach. Not in a kayak.
say.nudge: Come and see me, kid. I got that page dried out.
say.done: Thirty years of stories, and it turns out he was only ever doing his job.

replies: Barnaby? So he's got a name.
I'm listening.
Then we need a boat.

quests.title: Motorboat Savings
quests.card: Tag and release 8 deep-hole fish
quests.player: Am I ready for the Motorboat?

say.brief: Tag eight more deep-water fish. Get it logged, and you'll hit one thousand dollars - enough to buy my brand new motorboat!
say.nudge: Eight deep-water fish and that motorboat's yours.
say.done: A thousand dollars, kid. That is the motorboat paid for, whenever you want to sign for her.

quests.title: Buying the Motorboat
quests.card: Buy the Motorboat ($1,000)
quests.player: So I can take her anywhere now, right?

say.brief: She's all yours! A real motorboat with a steering wheel and a throttle. But listen to me very carefully, kid. Stay away from the center fog. The water out there drops into an abyssal trench over one hundred and twenty feet deep. No boat engine has survived out there in thirty years!
say.nudge: A thousand dollars, and she's yours. Come to the counter.
say.done: She is fuelled and tied off at the end of the boards. And kid - I meant every word about the middle of this lake.

replies: So I can take her anywhere now, right?
Understood. Nowhere near the fog.

quests.title: Walt's Warning Ignored
quests.card: Drive the Motorboat into the 120 ft trench fog
quests.player: ...I'll be careful, Walt.

say.brief: I know that look, kid. You are going to go and see for yourself, aren't you. Everybody does. Go on then - but keep her slow, keep your eyes up, and if that engine so much as coughs out there, you sit tight and you get on the radio. I will come and get you.
say.nudge: Well - you'll find out what's in that fog soon enough.
say.done: I told you, kid! I warned ya! I'm glad you're not hurt, but look at that motorboat stern - the propeller drive pin is snapped clean off, and the engine is dead. I towed you back, but that repair tab is gonna cost ya. You didn't hit a rock out there... Barnaby stopped your boat!

replies: ...I'll be careful, Walt.

quests.title: Kayak Recon
quests.card: Take the Kayak to the fog edge and magnet-fish where the motorboat stalled out
quests.player: What am I magnet-fishing for out in the fog?

say.brief: Barnaby doesn't mind kayaks - no noisy motors! Take your kayak back out to the edge of the fog where your boat broke down. Magnet-fish right where you stalled out. There's gotta be one last piece of the puzzle down there!
say.nudge: Right where you stalled. The kayak won't bother him.
say.done: The winding key. Well I never - that is the last of them, kid. Bring it here and let me see the lot together.

quests.title: Piecing It Together
quests.card: Bring the Lockbox blueprint to Walt
quests.player: What were all these brass parts for?

say.brief: You found the winding key! And look at this paper from the 1994 lockbox... it's a blueprint schematic! Kid! The brass frame, the gears, the sound comb, the winding key... we haven't been building a random music box on my counter... we've been building the old Warden's Acoustic Sonar!
say.nudge: Bring me that blueprint from the lockbox, kid.
say.done: A blueprint. Thirty years and the answer was in a box on the bottom of the lake. Right - I am going to need iron.

replies: What were all these brass parts for?
He built it to talk to him. That is what it was always for.

quests.title: Assembling the Sonar
quests.card: Trade 3 heavy scrap pieces to complete the Acoustic Sonar
quests.player: Will this sonar keep Barnaby calm?

say.brief: Hand me those three heavy scrap metal pieces! I'm using the brass from Big Mac's old prop to forge the outer housing.
say.nudge: Three heavy pieces of scrap and I'll forge the housing.
say.done: Done! The Acoustic Sonar is mounted right to your motorboat stern. Instead of noisy motor vibrations, it sends out gentle, warm musical chimes that Barnaby recognizes!

replies: Here you go - all three of them.

quests.title: The Cold Layer
quests.card: Tag three Cisco down in the cold layer, 50 ft or deeper
quests.player: Cisco? Where do they sit?

say.brief: One more thing before you go deep again. Every trout I have ever opened up out there had the same fish in it - cisco. Lake herring. Little silver things down in the cold layer. Fifty feet and below, on live shiners. Three of them tagged, kid, and then I will know what the trout are living on out there.
say.nudge: Three cisco, down in the cold layer. Fifty feet and below.
say.done: Three cisco. That is the bottom of the whole food chain out there, written down at last - and it explains the size of what is eating them.

quests.title: Deep Sanctuary Survey
quests.card: Tag and release 3 Lake Trout at 90 ft near the fog boundary
quests.player: Heading out to ninety feet now!

say.brief: Take this Pro Rod. While I do the final electrical wiring checks on the sonar, take your motorboat to the fog boundary and tag three deep lake trout at ninety feet.
say.nudge: Three trout at ninety feet, on the Pro Rod.
say.done: Three lake trout off the bottom at ninety feet, all three tagged and back in the cold. Nobody has that data, kid. Nobody.

quests.title: Pro Rod Mastery
quests.card: Tag and release a Lake Trout over 15 lbs down at 80 ft or deeper
quests.player: A fifteen-pounder, down in the cold.

say.brief: One more piece of rod work and we are done with it. There is an old lake trout down in that trench that will go fifteen pounds - eighty feet and better, right down in the cold. That Pro Rod was built for exactly that fish. Tag her, put her straight back, and I will have the last of my numbers.
say.nudge: There's a fifteen-pounder down at a hundred feet. Let the rod do the work.
say.done: A fifteen-pound lake trout from a hundred feet down! Wow! That Pro Rod handled the line tension beautifully. You've become a master angler, kid. Truly. That is a proper day's data, kid. Now then - that repair tab of yours. Those tag bounties will square it.

replies: A fifteen-pounder, down in the cold. I will find her.

quests.title: Cleared Tabs
quests.card: Pay off every dollar of the repair tab
quests.player: All tabs cleared! What's next?

say.brief: Every single dollar of your repair debt is paid off from your tag bounties! You're completely square with the shop, Junior Warden.
say.nudge: Square the tab and we're ready.
say.done: Not a dollar owing. You and me are square, kid - and I am glad it was you that pulled all this up.

replies: Feels good, being square.

quests.title: Final Checks
quests.card: Equip the Heavy Magnet with the Pro Rod and the Acoustic Sonar
quests.player: I'm ready to enter the Abyssal Trench.

say.brief: Heavy magnet equipped, Pro Rod ready, Acoustic Sonar online. Head out to the center fog in one hundred and twenty feet of water. Cut your engine, turn on the Acoustic Sonar, and let the music play into the water. Good luck, kid.
say.nudge: Heavy magnet, Pro Rod, sonar. Then the fog.
say.done: Everything checks out. Take her out, kid, and let us hear what he makes of it.

quests.title: The Chime on the Water
quests.card: Motor into the 120 ft trench, cut the engine and play the sonar
quests.player: I will call you when the sonar is down.

say.brief: Right then. That is everything, and it is all aboard. Out to the middle, kid, cut your engine, and let the sonar play down into it. I will have the radio on beside me the whole time - whatever happens out there, you are not out there on your own.
say.nudge: Cut the engine out there and let the sonar play.
say.done: You SAW him. After thirty years of stories, somebody finally saw him - and he came up to look at you. Sit down a minute, kid, before you tell me the rest.

replies: I will call you when the sonar is down.

quests.title: Passing the Torch
quests.card: Motor out to the trench and ring the Warden's bell where he can hear it

reward.title: Chief Junior Warden of Whispering Lake

quests.player: What do I do when I find him?

say.brief: Then go back out there and meet him properly. Take the sonar, take your time, and whatever he does - let him do it. I will be right here on the radio.
say.nudge: Take the bell, kid. He's offering it to you.
say.done: He did it! Barnaby knows the lake is in good hands now! From this day on, the deep center is an official Wildlife Sanctuary, and you are officially the Chief Junior Warden of Whispering Lake! I'm so proud of you, kid!

quests.title: What The Jam Kept
quests.card: Catch all ten fish that are in no book - any lure, anywhere
quests.player: The fog's gone? I thought that jam would be there for ever.

say.brief: Sit down a minute, Chief Warden. Something has happened out there. That fog is off the water for the first time since I was your age, and Barnaby has pulled the whole log jam apart - shoved it clean off the channel like it was brush. Which means the lake is calm, kid. All of it. No fog, no timber, no hull getting chewed up just for being out in the deep - you can go anywhere on this water now and take your time about it. And I will tell you what I think is out there. Thirty years shut behind that jam, nothing fished, nothing counted - there could be a dozen fish in this lake that are not in any book I own. So go and find them. Every lure in that box, every corner of the water, and no map for it - I have not got one. Ten of them, kid. Catch all ten and report back to me.
say.nudge: Ten fish nobody has in a book. Every lure, every corner - and no, I cannot tell you where.
say.done: Ten. TEN fish, and not one of them in a book on my shelf - a perch with no colour in it, a pike crossed with something, and a blue pike that has been extinct since before you were born. This is not a logbook any more, kid. This is a paper.

quests.title: Everything Somebody Lost
quests.card: Bring up all ten unique finds on the Heavy Magnet
quests.player: Everything's still down there?

say.brief: One more thing, and it is the last I will ask of you. That bottom out there has been shut away since the sixties, and everything that ever went over the side of a boat is still lying on it. Heavy magnet, kid. That is the only thing that will lift what I am after. Ten unique things - not scrap, not tin cans. Things somebody lost and wanted back. They will be a long time coming. They are lying anywhere at all and there is one of each, so when you have got one that is the only one there is. Bring me all ten.
say.nudge: Heavy magnet, and ten unique things off the bottom. Take your time.
say.done: All ten. A locket with a face still in it, a watch stopped at twenty past four, and a set of tags I am going to drive round to a house tonight. You gave this lake its memory back, kid. Go on - go fishing. It is yours now.

walt.q01a: Well, hey there, kid! Welcome to Whispering Lake Research and Tackle. Don't see many new faces down at the dock this early in the morning.
walt.q01b: They'll tell you the lake's cursed. Something big out in the middle that takes the propeller clean off a boat. I stopped arguing about it years ago. So this is a research station now: I study what's in the water, and I write up what I find.
walt.q01c: Five bucks, huh? Everybody starts somewhere. What I need is a pair of young hands - we catch them, tag them, log them and put every one straight back. Nothing gets kept on my dock. Start me here: my survey tank's empty and I need to know what's growing along the shore this year. Take this hand net, scoop me up thirty minnows and shiners - a netful at a time - and I'll pay you twenty-five dollars cash. Deal?
walt.q01d: Hold on, one more thing before you go. Here's a map of the lake - take it, you're gonna need it. Whole thing's on there: the shoreline, the bay, the drop-off, and the deep water out in the middle. It won't tell you where the fish are. Nothing will. But it'll stop you getting turned around out there, and on this lake that matters.
walt.q02a: Look at all those minnows! Fantastic work, kid - that's my survey tank stocked for the season. Here's your twenty-five dollars cash, fair and square.
walt.q02b: You can use that money right now to buy this bamboo rod and a container of earthworms. Now, see these sunfish hanging around the dock? We don't keep 'em to eat - we tag 'em! Catch three sunfish, clip a field tag on their fin, and let 'em go. Bring me the tag data when you're done.
walt.q03a: Logbook updated! Excellent work. You've got a real gentle touch with those fish, kid.
walt.q03b: Next up: yellow perch! They love hiding right next to the wooden dock pilings. Catch and tag three of 'em so we can track how fast they're growing this summer.
walt.q04a: Logbook updated! Perfect. Hey, while you're standing out on the dock, look down near the reed beds. Someone left a bunch of floating trash!
walt.q04b: Grab your hand net and scoop out five pieces of litter. We keep this water clean so the baby fish have a safe place to grow.
walt.q05a: Thanks for clearing out that trash. The lake looks better already, and I put twelve bucks in your hand for the trouble.
walt.q05b: You're moving fast, Junior Warden! Tag five more mixed panfish off the dock edge. Once that data's logged, you'll have enough cash to put a deposit down on my rental canoe and get off this dock!
walt.q06a: Five panfish tagged and logged - and that's your deposit money, kid. Twenty dollars puts the oars in your hands and that red canoe at the end of the slip is yours for the day. Say the word and she's yours.
walt.q06b: Head out into Shallow Bay, near the lily pads in fifteen feet of water. Largemouth bass love ambush hunting under those big green leaves. Tag two of 'em and bring back the log!
walt.q07a: Two largemouth bass, healthy and tagged! Outstanding.
walt.q07b: Black crappies travel in schools near the outer weed edges in twenty feet of water. Paddle out steady, drop your line right along the weedline, and tag four of 'em for the sanctuary database.
walt.q08a: Before you paddle back out, take this - Magnet Lure Number One! It attaches right to your line.
walt.q08b: Drop it over the shallow scrap markers out in the bay. People have been dropping iron and lost gear in this lake for fifty years. Pull me up three pieces of scrap metal, and I'll clean those scuffs off your canoe for free!
walt.q09a: Whoa! Hold on a second... where did you pull this up?!
walt.q09b: Look at those blade marks! This bronze propeller belonged to Big Mac's speedboat back in 2008. He used to tear through those shallow weeds like he owned the place, scaring off all the spawning bass.
walt.q09c: Big Mac swore a lake monster bit his boat! But look closely - Old Whisper didn't bite it. He jammed a thick, hardened tree root straight into the drive pin! Stopped his motor dead and taught Mac a lesson. Keep your eyes open out there, kid...
walt.q10a: I put that prop in the scrap bin - we can reuse that brass! Now, back to business.
walt.q10b: There's a giant five-pound largemouth bass lurking in the deepest lily pads on the west side. Set your hook clean, tag her up, and let her go!
walt.q11a: What in the world... let me see that!
walt.q11b: It's caked in lake mud, but under the grime... that's solid brass. It looks like a frame for some old mechanical device. See these mounting brackets?
walt.q11c: I'm setting this right here on the corner of my workbench in a tray of oil to soak off the rust. Whatever this was... it didn't sink by accident.
walt.q12a: The sun's getting low over the trees, kid. Perfect timing for catfish!
walt.q12b: Channel catfish feed along the muddy shallow banks right around dusk. Get two of 'em tagged and logged before you head into the dock for the night.
walt.q13b: Hey, if you've got five pieces of scrap metal in your inventory from magnet-fishing, trade 'em to me at the counter. I'll give you fifty dollars of shop credit toward your gear!
walt.q14a: You're doing great, kid. You're almost there!
walt.q14b: Tag and release six more shallow bay fish. Once that's logged, you'll have enough cash to buy your very own yellow Kayak! No more paying daily canoe rentals.
walt.q15a: She's all yours! That yellow Kayak is sleek, fast, and can handle deeper water.
walt.q15b: She'll easily take you past the thirty-five-foot drop-off. Just keep an eye on her hull durability bar down at the bottom of your screen. Hitting submerged logs out there will scuff her up, but you can always bring her back to me for repairs!
walt.q16a: Welcome to the Deep Hole, kid! The bottom drops like a cliff right past those buoys, all the way down to seventy-five feet.
walt.q16b: Northern pike hang on the weed edge and follow the break down - thirty-five to forty-five feet is as deep as they go. Paddle out, work the edge, and tag two of them for me.
walt.q17a: Those northern pike put up a real fight, didn't they? Great tags.
walt.q17b: Drop your line to the bottom in forty feet. Catfish are a warmwater fish - they hold on the mud above the cold layer and will not go down into it, whatever anybody tells you. Tag three of the big ones for me.
walt.q18b: These gear teeth match the brass frame you found earlier! Look - they interlock perfectly! Whoever built this knew exactly what they were doing. Let me mount these cogs right inside the frame...
walt.q19a: You've been putting some miles on that kayak, kid! See those scuffs on the bottom?
walt.q19b: Bring her up to the dock workshop. A little resin patch and some scrap metal will have her running smooth again. Give it a shot!
walt.q20b: There is a ten-pounder working the outside weed line in forty feet of water - the old ones drop down the break as the day warms. Tag her and let her go, and mind your line.
walt.q21a: Kid... would you look at these. Fine little metal tines, packed in tight — that's not scrap, that's a comb out of a music box.
walt.q21b: Pluck one and it hums way down low, lower than anything I'd tune for a tune. This wasn't built to play for people. Somebody built this to talk to something underwater.
walt.q22a: Whoa — hold on, let me get a grip on that. That is heavy for a box that size.
walt.q22b: Would you look at that seal, stamped right into the lid. Lake Warden, nineteen ninety-four. This has been sitting down there since the flood took the station.
walt.q22c: There's a journal in here, kid. Water's got into it, but I can just make out the last page... 'The flood of ninety-four sank our underwater sanctuary station. My loyal sturgeon stayed behind to guard the baby fish. I call him...' ...and that's as far as I can get. Rest of the page is stuck together. Give me tonight to dry it out proper before it falls apart in my hands.
walt.q23a: Kid! Dried that page out overnight, careful as I could. Warden's own hand, plain as day: 'I call him Barnaby.' Barnaby. That's not what you name a monster.
walt.q23b: Thirty years we've all been calling him Old Whisper, blaming him for every snapped line and every bad night out there — and near as I can tell, he's just an old sturgeon doing exactly what he was told to do back in ninety-four. Guarding this place.
walt.q24a: Logbook updated! You're doing incredible work out there.
walt.q24b: Tag eight more deep-water fish. Get it logged, and you'll hit one thousand dollars - enough to buy my brand new motorboat!
walt.q25a: She's all yours! A real motorboat with a steering wheel and a throttle.
walt.q25b: But listen to me very carefully, kid. Stay away from the center fog. The water out there drops into an abyssal trench over one hundred and twenty feet deep. No boat engine has survived out there in thirty years!
walt.q26a: I told you, kid! I warned ya!
walt.q26b: I'm glad you're not hurt, but look at that motorboat stern - the propeller drive pin is snapped clean off, and the engine is dead. I towed you back, but that repair tab is gonna cost ya. You didn't hit a rock out there... Barnaby stopped your boat!
walt.q27a: Barnaby doesn't mind kayaks - no noisy motors! Take your kayak back out to the edge of the fog where your boat broke down.
walt.q27b: Magnet-fish right where you stalled out. There's gotta be one last piece of the puzzle down there!
walt.q28a: You found the winding key! And look at this paper from the 1994 lockbox... it's a blueprint schematic!
walt.q28b: Kid! The brass frame, the gears, the sound comb, the winding key... we haven't been building a random music box on my counter... we've been building the old Warden's Acoustic Sonar!
walt.q29a: Hand me those three heavy scrap metal pieces! I'm using the brass from Big Mac's old prop to forge the outer housing.
walt.q29b: Done! The Acoustic Sonar is mounted right to your motorboat stern. Instead of noisy motor vibrations, it sends out gentle, warm musical chimes that Barnaby recognizes!
walt.q30a: Take this Pro Rod. While I do the final electrical wiring checks on the sonar, take your motorboat to the fog boundary and tag three deep lake trout at ninety feet.
walt.q31a: A fifteen-pound lake trout from a hundred feet down! Wow! That Pro Rod handled the line tension beautifully.
walt.q31b: You've become a master angler, kid. Truly.
walt.q32a: Every single dollar of your repair debt is paid off from your tag bounties! You're completely square with the shop, Junior Warden.
walt.q33a: Heavy magnet equipped, Pro Rod ready, Acoustic Sonar online.
walt.q33b: Head out to the center fog in one hundred and twenty feet of water. Cut your engine, turn on the Acoustic Sonar, and let the music play into the water. Good luck, kid.
walt.q34a: I hear the sonar chimes echoing through my shop radio, kid... low and warm. Keep steady out there.
walt.q34b: Look at your sonar screen... a massive shadow is rising from a hundred feet down... it's him!
walt.q35c: He did it! Barnaby knows the lake is in good hands now! From this day on, the deep center is an official Wildlife Sanctuary, and you are officially the Chief Junior Warden of Whispering Lake! I'm so proud of you, kid!
walt.q01a2: Truth be told, I don't see many faces at all any more. Folks still buy their line and their hooks off me - I'm cheaper than town - but they don't fish here. Look out there. Not one boat on the water. Not any more.
walt.q01b2: And what I'd give to know what's down in the middle, where it drops past a hundred feet. Nobody's been out there and come back with anything but a story.
walt.tackle_lost_1: Bare line, huh? No hook, no float, nothing. Yeah. THIS is why people don't come here any more, kid - they lose a rig, then another, and they go fish somewhere sensible. Here. New hook, new float, on me. Get back out there.
walt.tackle_lost_again: Again? Hm. Take another setup - no charge, I keep a drawer of them. Something strange about this water. One of these days I'd like to know what it is.
walt.q09_send: Big Mac lost something out by the west weed beds back in 2008 - swore blind a lake monster bit his boat, and he has never shut up about it since. Take the magnet out there and drag the bottom. I would dearly love to know what actually happened to that motor.
walt.q11_send: There's a shallow drop-off where the mud goes soft, and every so often somebody's magnet comes back heavier than it went down. Work that edge for me. Something metal is sitting in that mud, and I don't think it fell there on its own.
walt.q18_send: That brass frame has empty mountings in it, kid - whatever bolted into them is still down there. The drop-off is where the frame came from, so that's where the rest of it will be. Get the magnet down deep and drag it.
walt.q21_send: There's a log jam out in the deep water, and things collect in a log jam. If the rest of this machine went in where the frame did, the current will have walked it out that way. Take the magnet to the deep jam and see what comes up.
walt.q22_send: Seventy-five feet, kid - the deep edge. The old Warden's station went down somewhere along there in the flood, and a station means records. That's heavy magnet work and a long haul up, but if there's anything left of ninety-four, that's where it is.
walt.q08_done: Three good pieces of iron. Nice work with that magnet, kid.
walt.q10_done: Five pounds if she's an ounce, tagged and swimming. That's a proper bass, kid.
walt.q17_done: Three catfish off the mud and all three logged. You're getting the hang of the deep water.
walt.q20_done: A ten-pound pike off the deep weed edge! Tagged, logged and back in. That's the biggest thing in this lake with teeth - well, the biggest one anybody's ever landed.
walt.walt_log_1: In they go. Every one of them's in the book now, and every one of them's back in the water where I want it.
walt.walt_log_2: Logged, the lot of them. That's how a survey gets done, kid - one fish at a time, week after week.
walt.walt_log_3: Right. Names, lengths, weights, all of it down. You'd be amazed what a year of this tells you.
walt.walt_log_4: That's the record updated. Nobody else on this lake is writing any of this down, you know.
walt.walt_log_5: Good. The book's a little fatter than it was this morning.
walt.walt_logbig_1: Now that one's worth the ink. I'll put a star beside it.
walt.walt_logbig_2: Look at the size of that entry. Not many of those come across this counter, kid.
walt.walt_logbig_3: Well now. That one's going in underlined.
walt.walt_logmany_1: You have been busy! Hold on, let me turn the page.
walt.walt_logmany_2: That's a proper day's work. My hand's going to ache writing this lot up.
walt.walt_logmany_3: All of them? Good grief. Right - one at a time.
walt.walt_logone_1: One's one, kid. The book doesn't care how fast you fill it.
walt.walt_logone_2: In it goes. Small entries add up.
walt.walt_hold_1: You've got a boat full there. Bring them here and I'll get them logged.
walt.walt_hold_2: Something in the boat, I see. Let's have them in the book.
walt.walt_hold_3: Ah, you've been out. Hand them over and I'll write them up.
walt.q23_send: While I work on that page, there's a survey I keep putting off. Lake trout - cold-water fish, down below the thermocline where it stays cold all summer, and they will not come up for anybody. Seventy feet, kid. Tag two of them for me and put them back, and I should have something to tell you in the morning.
walt.q23c: Which means whatever is left of that station is still out in the middle of this lake, and the middle is the one part of it neither of us can reach. Not in a kayak.
walt.walt_done_1: That's the job done, kid. Let's settle up.
walt.walt_done_2: Well now. That is exactly what I asked for. Bring it here and we'll square it away.
walt.walt_done_3: Job's done, and done properly. Let's get you paid.
walt.q23_done: Thirty years of stories, and it turns out he was only ever doing his job.
walt.q14_done: That is the money, kid - enough for the kayak. She is tied up at the end of the boards whenever you are ready for her.
walt.q24_done: A thousand dollars, kid. That is the motorboat paid for, whenever you want to sign for her.
walt.q25_done: She is fuelled and tied off at the end of the boards. And kid - I meant every word about the middle of this lake.
walt.q31_done: That is a proper day's data, kid. Now then - that repair tab of yours. Those tag bounties will square it.
walt.q33_done: Everything checks out. Take her out, kid, and let us hear what he makes of it.
walt.walt_grant: Saving up for that? I have it right here.
walt.walt_scales: Great catch! Let's have a look at those.
walt.walt_bought_hand: Good choice. That is the one in your hands now.
walt.walt_bought_boat: Good choice. That is on your boat now.
walt.q27_done: The winding key. Well I never - that is the last of them, kid. Bring it here and let me see the lot together.
walt.q28_done: A blueprint. Thirty years and the answer was in a box on the bottom of the lake. Right - I am going to need iron.
walt.q30_done: Three lake trout off the bottom at ninety feet, all three tagged and back in the cold. Nobody has that data, kid. Nobody.
walt.q32_done: Not a dollar owing. You and me are square, kid - and I am glad it was you that pulled all this up.
walt.q34_done: You SAW him. After thirty years of stories, somebody finally saw him - and he came up to look at you. Sit down a minute, kid, before you tell me the rest.
walt.q35_send: Then go back out there and meet him properly. Take the sonar, take your time, and whatever he does - let him do it. I will be right here on the radio.
walt.q17b_a: Now then. There is a fish out on that breakline I have got no numbers on at all - walleye. Eyes like a cat's, feeds when the light goes flat, and gone the second the sun comes out.
walt.q17b_b: Twenty feet down off the drop, kid. Two of them tagged and I will have something to write in the column that has been empty since ninety-four.
walt.q17b_nudge: Two walleye, out on the breakline, twenty feet down.
walt.q17b_done: Walleye. Both tagged, both back in. That column is not empty any more, and it is your handwriting in it.
walt.q29b_a: One more thing before you go deep again. Every trout I have ever opened up out there had the same fish in it - cisco. Lake herring. Little silver things down in the cold layer.
walt.q29b_b: Fifty feet and below, on live shiners. Three of them tagged, kid, and then I will know what the trout are living on out there.
walt.q29b_nudge: Three cisco, down in the cold layer. Fifty feet and below.
walt.q29b_done: Three cisco. That is the bottom of the whole food chain out there, written down at last - and it explains the size of what is eating them.
walt.q36_a: Sit down a minute, Chief Warden. Something has happened out there. That fog is off the water for the first time since I was your age, and Barnaby has pulled the whole log jam apart - shoved it clean off the channel like it was brush.
walt.q36_b: Which means the lake is calm, kid. All of it. No fog, no timber, no hull getting chewed up just for being out in the deep - you can go anywhere on this water now and take your time about it.
walt.q36_c: And I will tell you what I think is out there. Thirty years shut behind that jam, nothing fished, nothing counted - there could be a dozen fish in this lake that are not in any book I own.
walt.q36_d: So go and find them. Every lure in that box, every corner of the water, and no map for it - I have not got one. Ten of them, kid. Catch all ten and report back to me.
walt.q36_nudge: Ten fish nobody has in a book. Every lure, every corner - and no, I cannot tell you where.
walt.q36_done: Ten. TEN fish, and not one of them in a book on my shelf - a perch with no colour in it, a pike crossed with something, and a blue pike that has been extinct since before you were born. This is not a logbook any more, kid. This is a paper.
walt.q37_a: One more thing, and it is the last I will ask of you. That bottom out there has been shut away since the sixties, and everything that ever went over the side of a boat is still lying on it.
walt.q37_b: Heavy magnet, kid. That is the only thing that will lift what I am after. Ten unique things - not scrap, not tin cans. Things somebody lost and wanted back.
walt.q37_c: They will be a long time coming. They are lying anywhere at all and there is one of each, so when you have got one that is the only one there is. Bring me all ten.
walt.q37_nudge: Heavy magnet, and ten unique things off the bottom. Take your time.
walt.q37_done: All ten. A locket with a face still in it, a watch stopped at twenty past four, and a set of tags I am going to drive round to a house tonight. You gave this lake its memory back, kid. Go on - go fishing. It is yours now.
walt.q26_send: I know that look, kid. You are going to go and see for yourself, aren't you. Everybody does. Go on then - but keep her slow, keep your eyes up, and if that engine so much as coughs out there, you sit tight and you get on the radio. I will come and get you.
walt.q31_send: One more piece of rod work and we are done with it. There is an old lake trout down in that trench that will go fifteen pounds - eighty feet and better, right down in the cold. That Pro Rod was built for exactly that fish. Tag her, put her straight back, and I will have the last of my numbers.
walt.q34_send: Right then. That is everything, and it is all aboard. Out to the middle, kid, cut your engine, and let the sonar play down into it. I will have the radio on beside me the whole time - whatever happens out there, you are not out there on your own.

nudges.q01: No rush, kid. Thirty little fish - the shoreline's full of 'em.
nudges.q02: Three sunfish, tagged and let go. They're right under the boards.
nudges.q03: Perch hug those pilings. Three tags, and bring me the data.
nudges.q04: That litter's still floating by the reeds. Five pieces, kid.
nudges.q05: Five more panfish and that canoe deposit is yours.
nudges.q06: The bass are under the lily pads in fifteen feet. Two tags.
nudges.q07: Crappies run the outer weedline in twenty feet. Four of 'em.
nudges.q08: Drop that magnet over the scrap markers. Three pieces gets your canoe cleaned.
nudges.q09: Whatever's out by the west weeds, the magnet'll find it.
nudges.q10: She's a five-pounder, in the deepest pads on the west side. Take your time.
nudges.q11: Something's in the mud at the shallow drop-off. Keep dragging that magnet.
nudges.q12: Catfish come up the muddy banks at dusk. Two tags before dark.
nudges.q13: Five pieces of scrap at the counter, and it's fifty dollars of credit.
nudges.q14: Six more bay fish and that kayak's yours.
nudges.q15: The yellow kayak's two hundred and fifty. Come see me at the counter.
nudges.q16: Pike patrol the rock ledges past the buoys. Two tags, kid.
nudges.q17: Straight down to the mud at forty feet. Three big catfish.
nudges.q18: There's more of that brass down the drop-off. Keep the magnet down.
nudges.q19: Bring the kayak up to the workshop and we'll patch her.
nudges.q20: Ten-pounder, on the outside weed line in forty feet. Keep him out of the pads.
nudges.q21: Try the magnet at the deep log jam. Something's still down there.
nudges.q22: The seventy-five-foot edge, kid. Heavy magnet work.
nudges.q23: Two lake trout in seventy feet. Cold water, deep line.
nudges.q24: Eight deep-water fish and that motorboat's yours.
nudges.q25: A thousand dollars, and she's yours. Come to the counter.
nudges.q26: Well - you'll find out what's in that fog soon enough.
nudges.q27: Right where you stalled. The kayak won't bother him.
nudges.q28: Bring me that blueprint from the lockbox, kid.
nudges.q29: Three heavy pieces of scrap and I'll forge the housing.
nudges.q30: Three trout at ninety feet, on the Pro Rod.
nudges.q31: There's a fifteen-pounder down at a hundred feet. Let the rod do the work.
nudges.q32: Square the tab and we're ready.
nudges.q33: Heavy magnet, Pro Rod, sonar. Then the fog.
nudges.q34: Cut the engine out there and let the sonar play.
nudges.q35: Take the bell, kid. He's offering it to you.
